turns.zh: 公司们正在告别老旧技术、转向 Ridgeline，因为与投资管理软件里的其他产品相比，Ridgeline 的 AI 功能领先太多。

turns.en: I've been hearing from a lot of investment managers about AI and they fall roughly into two camps, with some unsure where to even start and others convinced they can build their own order management system over a weekend.
turns.zh: 我跟很多投资管理人聊过 AI，他们大致分两派：一派连从哪起步都不知道，另一派坚信自己周末就能搭出一套自己的订单管理系统。

turns.en: The reality is that running an investment firm will always require governance, controls, and a single source of truth for your data. And no amount of AI enthusiasm changes that requirement.
turns.zh: 现实是，经营一家投资公司，永远需要治理、控制和数据的单一真相源，再多的 AI 热情也改变不了这个要求。

turns.en: Ridgeline is built on exactly that foundation, which is why I believe that the firms that come out ahead in the AI era will be the ones running on Ridgeline's unified platform.
turns.zh: Ridgeline 正是建立在这个基础之上。所以我相信，AI 时代胜出的公司，会是那些跑在 Ridgeline 统一平台上的公司。

turns.en: If you're serious about your firm's AI strategy, Ridgeline should be part of that conversation and you can request a demo at ridgeline.ai. If I were to imagine an equivalent of me and an equivalent of you sitting somewhere in China today and I asked you the same question about how power is formed, what do you think they would say there under a very different system?
turns.zh: 如果你认真对待公司的 AI 战略，Ridgeline 应该是这场讨论的一部分，可以在 ridgeline.ai 预约演示。假如我想象今天的 China 某个地方，坐着一个『我』的翻版和一个『你』的翻版，我问他们同样关于权力如何形成的问题——在那样一套截然不同的制度下，你觉得他们会怎么回答？

turns.en: I used to have these conversations in China. Some of my books have been published in Chinese and I've gone to Chinese universities and had these conversations with scholars and officials.
turns.zh: 我以前在 China 做过这类对话。我的有几本书出了中文版，我去 China 的高校，和学者、官员聊过这些话题。

turns.en: Now what I can say is they are very aware of this dynamic. If they're things that keep Xi Jinping awake at night, I think one of them is his awareness that in any kind of conflict with the United States, China would face being cut off from so many of the raw materials and so on and markets that's economy needs.
turns.zh: 我能说的是，他们对这个动态非常清楚。如果有事情让 Xi Jinping 夜不能寐，我想其中之一就是他明白：在和美国的任何形式的冲突中，China 将面临被切断其经济所需要的众多原材料和市场的可能。

turns.en: I mean, let's imagine China declares a blockade of Taiwan, which could very easily happen. The United States just from 100 miles further out imposes a counter blockade on China.
turns.zh: 比如说，假设 China 宣布封锁 Taiwan——这完全可能发生——US 只要在 100 英里更外圈，对 China 反封锁就是了。

turns.en: Nothing is going in or, you know, no oil is coming in or out, no manufactured goods are being sold, what happens to the Chinese economy, all the soybean contracts they have with farmers in Brazil and Argentina not getting delivered.
turns.zh: 什么都进不来——石油进不来也出不去，制成品卖不出去——China 经济会怎么样？他们和 Brazil、Argentina 豆农签的大豆合同全都无法交付。

turns.en: We've all been surprised with the Iran war to see just how big the Chinese oil stockpiles have become. A lot of Chinese energy policy can be understood as trying to avoid the trap of dependence on the global economy.
turns.zh: Iran 战争让大家吃惊地看到，China 的石油储备已经堆到了多大的规模。China 的很多能源政策，其实都可以理解为在规避『依赖全球经济』这个陷阱。

turns.en: They're doing the solar, they're doing as much hydro as they can and some of our friends in the environmental movement are saying, oh, it's so wonderful, they're so green.
turns.zh: 他们搞光伏，尽可能多地搞水电，我们环保运动的一些朋友就说：哇，太好了，他们多绿色啊。

turns.en: Let's cooperate with China to build a new world. They're also digging as much coal as they possibly can because what they're trying to do is make themselves less dependent on the outside world so that in a worst case scenario with the U.S., they can actually fight for the long term.
turns.zh: ——『让我们和 China 合作，建设一个新世界。』但他们也在拼命挖煤，因为他们在做的是让自己更少依赖外部世界，好跟 US 走到最坏情况时真的能撑长期。

turns.en: Do you think the U.S. runs the risk of trying to do that same thing, become more isolationist? Our exports are relatively low as a percent of GDP compared to lots of other countries throughout the world.
turns.zh: 你觉得 US 有没有也在冒同样的风险——想这么做，变得更孤立主义？相比世界上许多其他国家，我们的出口占 GDP 的比重相对较低。

turns.en: We are fairly self-sufficient. America is an amazing place, natural resource, rich, two oceans on either side, we have these amazing advantages.
turns.zh: 我们其实相当自给自足。America 是个了不起的地方，自然资源丰富，两边有大洋，我们有这些得天独厚的优势。

turns.en: Maybe we could do it without this interdependent thing that's created this amazing power structure as you laid out. Does that worry you that we trend more in the direction of being isolationist or something?
turns.zh: 也许我们不需要这套相互依存也能过——而正是这套相互依存塑造了你描述的惊人的权力结构。我们朝孤立主义方向滑，你会为此担忧吗？

turns.en: Well, I think, look, there is obviously in American history, we have a tradition of isolationism that is stronger at some times than others and it's definitely coming up now.
turns.zh: 我觉得，你看，US 历史里显然有孤立主义传统，有时强些有时弱些，而现在它确实在抬头。

turns.en: And it does worry me a good deal because I do think American security and the American economy do ultimately require us to be engaged globally, not necessarily as global social workers or something, but you think about our trade, roughly a third of it is in the hemisphere, a third of it across the Pacific, a third of it across the Atlantic.
turns.zh: 它确实让我很担忧，因为我确实认为，American 的安全和 American 经济终究要求我们全球参与——未必是当世界社工什么的。但看看我们的贸易：大约三分之一在西半球，三分之一跨 Pacific，三分之一跨 Atlantic。

turns.en: We couldn't really very easily do without any one of those. We saw during the pandemic that our dependence on China for all kinds of things was really quite alarming.
turns.zh: 这三块里缺了任何一块，我们都不容易过得下去。疫情期间我们看到，我们对 China 的各类依赖真挺触目惊心的。

turns.en: People look at our supply chains and they can see a lot of vulnerabilities. But we can't make everything that we need right here. We can't get all the raw materials that we need right here, but also our producers need more than the American market.
turns.zh: 人们看我们的供应链，能看到很多脆弱点。但我们不可能在这儿生产所有需要的东西，也不可能在这儿获得所有需要的原材料；而且我们的生产者需要的也不止 American 市场。

turns.en: Traditionally, the most free market lobby in the United States has been the agricultural lobby because America can do a lot more than feed ourselves.
turns.zh: 传统上，US 最倡导自由贸易的游说集团是农业游说团，因为 America 能做的远不止养活我们自己。

turns.en: Our farmers can feed practically the world and if they're reduced to only feeding the American market, they can't make money. The prices are so low.
turns.zh: 我们的农民几乎能养活全世界，如果他们只被允许供应 US 市场，他们赚不到钱——价格太低了。

turns.en: They need that market. The same is true. You know, there's so many economies of scale. If our AI companies, if our tech companies can only benefit from the internal American market, that's actually not enough to generate the revenue and growth that they need even to stay technologically equal, say to China, much less be ahead and be super profitable.
turns.zh: 他们需要世界市场。同样如此，你知道，这里有太多规模经济。如果我们的 AI 公司、科技公司只能从 US 内部市场获益，其实不足以产生所需的营收和增长——哪怕只想在技术上与 China 持平都不够，更别提保持领先、赚大钱了。

turns.en: Our business needs the world and then there's the question of, okay, well, you can't really make people buy your stuff at the point of a gun and you don't really want to have a gun around all the time.
turns.zh: 我们的企业需要世界。然后还有那个问题：你总不能拿枪逼着别人买你的东西，而你也不想时刻把枪带在身边。

turns.en: So you have to have a trading relationship that works for both sides. Both sides have to agree to the trade. There are ways of doing that. We got very doctrinaire in this belief that a simple free trade system would work.
turns.zh: 所以你得有一个对双方都行的贸易关系，双方都得同意这笔买卖。这有办法做到。我们之前变得很教条，相信一个简单纯粹的自由贸易体系就能运转。

turns.en: We didn't look for systematic cheating from China, but we also, after World War II particularly, a lot of the European countries were so poor and devastated from the war that reviving their economies became necessary for American security.
turns.zh: 我们没盯着 China 系统性的作弊行为；而且二战之后，尤其是许多 European 国家穷得被战争打残了，复兴他们的经济对 US 的安全而言成了必需。

turns.en: Otherwise, they would have gone communist and we didn't want that. So we said, okay, fine, Germany, you can have really high tariffs on American goods, but we won't reciprocate because it's in our interest for you to grow.
turns.zh: 否则他们就会倒向共产主义，而我们不想看到。于是我们就说：好吧，Germany，你可以对 US 商品征很高的关税，我们不报复，因为你成长起来符合我们的利益。

turns.en: A lot of that stuff got institutionalized. There are many, many cases now where you have non-reciprocal tariffs and our barriers have been lower.
turns.zh: 很多这类安排被制度化了。现在有许许多多非互惠关税的案例，而我们的壁垒一直更低。

turns.en: The Trump people were not wrong to say, okay, this needed to change. We're also seeing with the need for supply change security and so on. You can't simply take your economic policy out of a free trade textbook.
turns.zh: Trump 团队说『这得改变』，并没有错。我们还看到供应链安全之类的需要——你不能简单照搬自由贸易教科书来制定经济政策。

turns.en: On the other hand, you do still need trade. Trade needs to be beneficial on both ends. I want to talk about the changing orientation of us versus the world sort of our foreign policy, but first ask about technology because when I started my career, I'm 41.
turns.zh: 但另一方面，你确实仍然需要贸易，贸易需要两端都受益。我想聊聊『US 对世界』这组关系的转变，也就是我们的外交政策取向，但先问技术这一块，因为我开始职业生涯的时候——我 41 岁。

turns.en: So 20 years ago, call it, I remember seeing, I've always been an investor, if you looked at the top 10 or 20 market cap companies, it was a total global mix of companies from many different industries.
turns.zh: 那是二十年前了吧。我记得——我一直是投资人——如果你去看市值前十或前二十的公司，那是一锅全球大杂烩，来自各行各业。

turns.en: It looked like this kind of potpourri list. Now that same list is literally just American technology companies, basically one through 20. There's a couple of exceptions.
turns.zh: 像一锅什锦拼盘。而今天同一份榜单，几乎清一色就是 US 科技公司，基本上从第一到第二十，就那么几个例外。

turns.en: It's more or less total dominance by American technology companies. And that was true before OpenAI and Anthropic and SpaceX. Now those are resurgent even on top of our great technology companies.
turns.zh: 可以说是 US 科技公司的绝对统治。这在 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 和 SpaceX 之前就已经成立；而如今，这些公司即便在我们一众伟大的科技公司之上也来势汹汹。

turns.en: And I'd love to just hear you reflect on how tech, of course AI, you have to ask about that as well, are changing the nature of global order in such a digitally dominant set of technologies that we're once again the leader in.
turns.zh: 我很想听听你的思考：技术——当然还有 AI，这是必须问的——如何改变全球秩序的本质，我们再一次在这样一套数字上占绝对主导的技术里处于领先。你怎么消化这件事？

turns.en: How do you process it? I do try to look to historical analogies. There's nothing exactly the same as this. The closest you really can see is to the actual industrial revolution, interestingly the country that led the first industrial revolution, Britain, then dominated for 150 years, became a dominant power.
turns.zh: 我确实会去找历史类比。没有任何事情和这个完全一样。最接近的，其实是真正的工业革命。有趣的是，领导第一次工业革命的国家——Britain——随后主导了 150 年，成为霸权国。

turns.en: History is moving a lot faster now, but I think we absolutely have been in this position of the first to really see and use this potential source of power.
turns.zh: 现在历史节奏快得多，但我认为我们完全处在『第一个真正看见并利用这股潜在权力之源』的位置上。

turns.en: I think since the 17th century, the key to power in the modern world is which countries can be most effective at developing, harnessing, exploiting the power of new technology without blowing up internally because of the social stress and upheavals that new technology causes.
turns.zh: 我想，从 17 世纪起，现代世界权力的关键就在于：哪些国家能最高效地开发、驾驭、利用新技术的力量，同时不因为新技术带来的社会压力与动荡而在内部炸锅。

turns.en: And for a lot of reasons, I think first the British and then we were just better at riding that wild horse than other people were. I think that is still true, but you can look at American society today and see the reaction against tech, this sort of anti-data center thing.
turns.zh: 出于种种原因，我想先是 British、然后是我们，就是比别人更会驯那匹野马。我认为这仍然成立。但你看今天的 US 社会，能看到对技术的反弹——这种反数据中心的情绪。

turns.en: And we've got Trotskyites in the DSA thinking that the most retrograde forms of Marxism are our only salvation in this terrible situation. It's not a given that we will be able to pull it off again.
turns.zh: 而且 DSA（美国民主社会主义者）里还有一群托派，认为最落后的那些马克思主义形态，才是这个糟糕处境的唯一救赎。我们能不能再次得手，并非板上钉钉。

turns.en: Enormous progress and yet total chaos and dissension. The relationship between achievement and order right now has broken down because we need a different kind of order than we've had because our technology has created a new kind of world.
turns.zh: 巨大的进步，却伴随彻底的混乱和分裂。成就与秩序之间的关系目前破裂了——因为我们需要的秩序，和我们过去拥有的不一样了，因为我们的技术已经创造了一个新型的世界。

turns.en: It is changing the way power works. It is changing the nature of power. So far, America is doing what we've been doing for a very long time, which is dominating the cutting edge.
turns.zh: 它在改变权力运作的方式，也在改变权力的本质。到目前为止，US 还在做我们做了很久的事：主导最前沿。

turns.en: So we've developed it. We have the horse. It's the key to riding the wild horse because I think everyone in America would say, yeah, I hope the next 150 years we dominate and it's because...
turns.zh: 所以我们发展了它，我们有了这匹马。它正是驯服野马的关键。因为我想，每个 US 人都会说：是啊，希望未来 150 年还是我们主导，而这要归因于……

turns.en: But in a nice way. Because that's the kind of people we are. How would you have us do that? What are the keys to doing that well now that we have the horse?
turns.zh: ——要用一种好的方式，因为我们是那种人。你会希望我们怎么做？既然我们已经有这匹马，要把这件事做好的关键是什么？

turns.en: America has always been an ownership society. Why did a lot of the founders think that the United States could survive as a reasonably democratic republic?
turns.zh: US 一直以来都是一个有产社会（ownership society）。为什么很多开国者认为，United States 能够作为一个相当民主的共和国存续下来？

turns.en: And one of the big answers was instead of being a country of people who lived in cities and basically owned nothing and worked for other people, America was by and large a country of independent farmers who were kind of small business people and who owned their own land, had a stake in the system and their life experience as an owner teaches them citizenship.
turns.zh: 一个重要的答案是：US 不是一个人们住在城里、几乎一无所有、给他人打工的国家，而大体上是一个独立农民的国家——他们有点像小生意人，拥有自己的土地，在这个体系里有切身利益；作为所有者的经历，教会了他们什么是公民。

turns.en: So boy, I really would love to see a new bridge over the stream here. On the other hand, if they build that, they're going to have to raise my taxes.
turns.zh: 哎呀，我真想在这条小河上建一座新桥。可话说回来，要是真建了，就得给我加税。

turns.en: I then calculate in a rational way what I would like to happen. And that is the kind of political education that prepares me to take a thoughtful role in the councils of the country, plus I'm independent.
turns.zh: 然后我用理性的方式盘算我希望事情怎样发生。这就是一种政治教育，让我准备好在国家的议事中扮演一个深思熟虑的角色——而且我是独立的。

turns.en: And then with the industrial revolution, can this continue? We're getting the big cities. We're getting industry. Well, the first stage we do with the railroads and the Homestead Act, they kind of come in together.
turns.zh: 然后工业革命来了，这还能延续吗？大城市来了，工业来了。第一阶段，我们靠铁路和《宅地法》（Homestead Act），两者几乎是一起进来的。

turns.en: The government gives a ton of land in often somewhat corrupt ways to railroads, to build transcontinental railroads that turn the country into a national market, but then also gives free land to the American farmer.
turns.zh: 政府以往往有点腐败的方式把海量土地拨给铁路公司，让他们修建横贯大陆的铁路，把这个国家变成一个全国市场；同时，又给 US 农民免费发土地。

turns.en: You go live on your farm for five years and it's yours. Amazing. For the ordinary person, all right, I'm getting a free farm out of the system.
turns.zh: 你去自己的农庄住上五年，它就是你的了。太了不起了。对普通人来说：行，我从这个体系里白得了一个农庄。

turns.en: I'm a farmer. And yet you're doing this in a way that is simultaneously allowing the infrastructure of a new industrial society to take place.
turns.zh: 我成了农民。而与此同时，你做的这一切恰恰让一个新工业社会的基础设施得以落地。

turns.en: To get in the 20th century, think about how as the family farm begins to decay economically, it can't compete. You have to be very well-capitalized to farm under modern conditions and so on.
turns.zh: 到了 20 世纪，你可以想想：家庭农场开始在经济上衰落、竞争不过去了，在现代农业条件下你得有充沛的资本才能务农，如此等等。

turns.en: And where people are starting to work in cities and be employees, is this going to endanger the republic? Are we still going to be a free society of free people?
turns.zh: 而人们开始进城市当雇员，这会不会危及共和国？我们还能不能是一个自由人的自由社会？

turns.en: Essentially, we came up with the idea of the single-family home in the suburbs to replace the single-family farm. A lot of government policy was around, think about not only building the freeways and the highways, but subsidies to the tax code so that municipal bonds are tax-free, which means towns can build the infrastructure that you need to attract the developers and the homeowners who will then raise the value of the property and so you can repay the bonds out of the
turns.zh: 本质上，我们想出了在郊区建独栋住宅的主意，来取代独栋农场。大量的政府政策都围绕它——想想看，不仅是修高速公路和快速路，还有税法里的补贴，让市政债券免税。这就意味着城镇可以先行建设必要的基础设施，吸引开发商和房主进来，从而推高物业价值，然后你再用——

turns.en: higher property values that the infrastructure has created. So this kind of wealth-creating machine. Well, right now we seem to be in a place where we're reaching the limits of that wealth-creating machine because it's just too expensive for the average person to buy a house and land close enough to where you work so that the commute isn't killing you.
turns.zh: ——被基础设施创造出来的更高物业价值来偿还债券。这就是某种造富机器。而现在，我们似乎正逼近这台造富机器的极限：对普通人来说，在离工作地点足够近的地方买房置地实在太贵了——近到通勤不至于把人累死。

turns.en: You look at why are so many young people really unhappy with the way the economy is working. Home ownership is one of the real big problems.
turns.zh: 你看看，为什么这么多年轻人对经济的运转方式如此不满。住房自有率（home ownership）是真正的大问题之一。

turns.en: IT can kind of address this between remote work and hybrid work and self-driving cars. If you only have to go into work once or twice a week or twice a month or whatever, you can work farther out.
turns.zh: 信息技术多少能解决这个问题——远程办公、混合办公，再加上自动驾驶汽车。如果你一周只需要到岗一两次，或者一个月两次什么的，你就能住得更远。

turns.en: If you expand the commuting radius, say from 40 miles to 75 miles, the amount of land that is developable for housing goes up with the square of the radius, it's geometric.
turns.zh: 如果你把通勤半径从 40 英里扩大到 75 英里，可用于住房开发的土地量是按半径的平方增长的——是几何级的。

turns.en: So you can open information technology appropriately deployed, can open up for another two generations this wealth-creating machine. Is there something equivalent to Homestead or the subsidy of homes that could drive this expansion?
turns.zh: 所以，部署得当的 IT，能让这台造富机器再为两代人打开局面。有没有什么和《宅地法》或者住房补贴对等的东西，能驱动这一轮扩张？

turns.en: It seems like a really, really important thing to get right for America. I think so. I think we should be doing things like encouraging remote and hybrid work.
turns.zh: 对 US 来说，这似乎是一件真的、真的必须做对的大事。我也这么认为。我觉得我们应该做一些事，比如鼓励远程办公和混合办公。

turns.en: Now, there are problems with it, mentoring, there are benefits, fine. There are problems with every form of technology. How many people has the car killed since we started using cars?
turns.zh: 当然，它有问题——比如师徒传承（mentoring）会受影响——但也有好处，行。每一种技术都伴随着问题。自从我们用上汽车以来，它已经害死了多少人？

turns.en: How much money has it cost for the highway systems and so on? A new technology just doesn't appear like an angel and grant wishes everywhere.
turns.zh: 公路系统又花了多少钱？等等。一项新技术不会像天使一样降临、四处满足愿望。

turns.en: You have to think really hard about how to make it work. I think of this as info structure. Infrastructure is building the bridges and the physicals.
turns.zh: 你得非常认真去思考怎么让它运转起来。我把这叫做 info structure（信息基建）。Infrastructure（基础设施）是架桥和那些实体硬件。

turns.en: Info structure is the institutional legal regulatory framework that can allow AI technology to develop, give better results to patients in a hospital.
turns.zh: Info structure 则是让 AI 技术得以发展的制度、法律、监管框架——让医院里的病人得到更好的疗效。

turns.en: That's actually incredibly complicated or that could transform the legal system. Very complex stuff. You need a new kind of social imagination for that, which I think we need to develop.
turns.zh: 这件事其实极其复杂——或者说能改造整个法律体系，是非常复杂的东西。你需要一种新的社会想象力，我觉得这正是我们需要培养的。

turns.en: But in this housing example, if a company says, fine, you can stay home 60% of the time, that's less wear and tear on infrastructure, fewer needs for construction, a tax benefit for companies that move toward greater hybrid and remote work is not a net cost for government because in fact, you're saving on another part of the budget.
turns.zh: 但就拿住房这个例子来说，如果一家公司说『行，你 60% 的时间可以待在家』，那基础设施的磨损就小了，建设的需要就少了。给朝更大程度混合办公和远程办公靠拢的公司以税收优惠，对政府来说并不是净成本，因为实际上你在预算的另一头省了钱。

turns.en: This technology seems so unique because, and I'm curious what you think about it, in the case of AI, we've seen with China, it seems to be the other great power today, that through using our technology that we've invested in, they're able to distill would be the term in the AI world and have fairly comparable systems without the capital investment, which is very different than the highway system or the railroads.
turns.zh: 这项技术看起来如此独特，因为——我也好奇你怎么看——在 AI 这件事上，我们看到作为今天另一个大国的 China，通过利用我们投资出来的技术，就能——AI 圈的说法是『蒸馏』（distill）——造出相当有竞争力的系统，而不用相应的资本投入。这和公路系统或铁路非常不同。

turns.en: You can't copy those things, you have to do it yourself, and so the economy of scale is easier for me to get my head around when it's a railroad than when it's a frontier lab model or something like this, which makes me wonder about the right kind of foreign policy, and it's a good excuse to talk about your four kinds of American foreign policy historically.
turns.zh: 那些东西你抄不了，只能自己干。所以，当它是铁路时，规模经济我比较好理解；当它是 frontier lab（前沿实验室）的模型这种东西，我就不好理解了。这让我开始思索什么样的外交政策是对的，而这正好也是聊聊你提出的、历史上美国四种外交政策的由头。

turns.en: Maybe you could just quickly tick through them and outline them as an intro before we talk about that notion of tech Hamiltonians that I thought was quite interesting of yours.
turns.zh: 也许你可以先快速过一遍、勾个轮廓作为引子，然后我们再谈『科技汉密尔顿主义者』（tech Hamiltonians）这个概念——我觉得你这个提法特别有意思。

turns.en: One of the interesting things about America is that our foreign policy arguments are very repetitive. Basically, if something comes up in foreign policy, we'll argue about it in many of the same ways they would have done in George Washington's day.
turns.zh: US 有意思的一点是：我们的外交政策争论非常重复。基本上，外交上出一件事，我们会用的那些争法，和 George Washington 时代的人会用的差不多。

turns.en: Our views of the country and of foreign policy fairly predictably fall into one of four baskets. One is what I do call Hamiltonian, Alexander Hamilton.
turns.zh: 我们对国家和外交政策的看法，可以相当有把握地归进四个篮子。一个是我所说的 Hamiltonian（汉密尔顿主义），来自 Alexander Hamilton。

turns.en: What you see is a strong capitalist economy that is trading effectively with the rest of the world provides the money and the technological progress that holds society together as people are making money at it and they're happy and also gives you the strength so that no other country can attack you.
turns.zh: 你看到的是：一个强大的资本主义经济体，有效地与世界其他地方贸易。它提供了维系社会的金钱与技术进步——大家在其中赚钱、皆大欢喜——同时也给你实力，让任何其他国家都不敢攻击你。

turns.en: We should have a strong federal government that does things like promote infrastructure at home, that sees itself as trying to help major American companies succeed internationally.
turns.zh: 我们应该有一个强有力的联邦政府，在国内推动基础设施，并且把自己看作要帮助 major American companies 成功走向国际的角色。

turns.en: George H.W. Bush in some ways. Then you have people who say, oh, money, that's just so vulgar. What about human rights? I would argue, you know, what causes the threats that America faces?
turns.zh: George H.W. Bush 在某种意义上就是这样。然后也有人说：哦，钱？太俗了。人权怎么办？

turns.en: Well, it's bad governance, dictatorship. Communities don't go to war, dictatorships do. Generals like to fight, moms don't. American foreign policy should be about promoting democracy globally, promoting international institutions.
turns.zh: 那源于糟糕的治理、独裁。共同体不会开战，独裁政权才会。将军们爱打仗，母亲们不爱。US 的外交政策应该致力于在全球推广民主，推广国际制度。

turns.en: Let's get rid of war by getting rid of the causes of war. And that's a kind of Wilsonian approach, which we certainly had actually long before Woodrow Wilson.
turns.zh: 铲除战争的根源，战争自会消失。这是某种 Wilsonian（威尔逊式）的路径——其实在 Woodrow Wilson 之前很久我们就有了。

turns.en: Then you've got people who say, wait a minute, the thing that's great about America is personal liberty. The fact that the government doesn't control us all and isn't taxing us to death.
turns.zh: 然后另一些人说：等等，US 的伟大之处是个人自由——政府没有管着我们所有人，也没有把税收到把我们逼死。

turns.en: If we get involved, whether it's these Wilsonian crusades for human rights or Hamiltonian great power balance of politics, international finance, what we're going to have is a powerful government that has secrets from the American people, runs colossal defense budgets, gets us into endless wars, and that will destroy the liberty.
turns.zh: 如果我们深陷其中——无论是这些 Wilsonian 的人权十字军，还是 Hamiltonian 的大国政治平衡、国际金融——我们得到的将是一个对 US 人民保守秘密、操持巨额国防预算、把我们拖入无尽战争的强权政府，而那将摧毁自由。

turns.en: We can conquer the world and lose our freedom at home. What kind of foreign policy is that? And again, we've been having this since the 1790s.
turns.zh: 我们可能征服了世界，却在国内失去了自由。这算什么外交政策？再次强调，这场争论我们从 1790 年代就有了。

turns.en: And then finally, there's the group I called Jacksonian after Andrew Jackson, who sort of say, well, listen, foreigners, they can be democratic.
turns.zh: 最后，还有一群人，我称之为 Jacksonian（杰克逊主义），得名自 Andrew Jackson。他们大致会说：好吧，听着，外国人——他们民主也好——

turns.en: I don't really care what the foreigners do. As long as you don't attack us or impugn our honor. If somebody attacks us, we should just go ahead and crush them and laws of war.
turns.zh: 我根本不在乎外国人干什么，只要你不打我们、不辱我们的名声。要是有人敢打我们，我们就直接碾碎他们——还谈什么战争法。

turns.en: No, like rats, you should exterminate them and you beat them and pound them and crush them until they understand that the last thing they should ever do is raise their hand against the United States.
turns.zh: 不，对待他们就像对付耗子，要消灭他们；要打他们、砸他们、碾他们，直到他们明白：天底下最不该做的事，就是对 United States 抬手动脚。

turns.en: And Jacksonians often look like Jeffersonians that isolationists in times of peace, but something happens like Pearl Harbor and 911. And suddenly the Jacksonians are activated.
turns.zh: 而在和平年代，Jacksonians 看上去往往像 Jeffersonians——孤立主义者。但一发生 Pearl Harbor、911 这样的事，Jacksonians 突然就被激活了。

turns.en: So I think we've been having these things for a very long time. We still have them today. I say these are like suits in a deck of cards. Very few of us have just like all 13 Hamiltonian cards.
turns.zh: 所以我想，这些争论我们已经打了很久，今天依然如此。我打个比方：它们就像一副牌里的四种花色。我们当中很少有人拿着一手清一色的 13 张 Hamiltonian 牌。

turns.en: We generally all have a mixed hand, but we tend to have some suits are stronger than others for each of us. Which of those suits do you think most defines us today?
turns.zh: 我们大体都是一手杂牌，只是对每个人来说，某些花色比别的更强。你觉得今天哪一种花色最能定义我们？

turns.en: Well, I think the old democratic consensus, let's say the Clinton consensus was very much a coalition of Wilson and Hamilton, build a global system that advances the country's economic security, but also promotes human rights and democracy.
turns.zh: 我想，老的民主党共识——比如说 Clinton 共识——很大程度上是 Wilson 和 Hamilton 的联盟：建一个既推进国家经济安全、又促进人权与民主的全球体系。

turns.en: And that will both make us rich and build a lasting global peace. That's been kind of the predominant establishment idea really since World War II.
turns.zh: 这既让我们致富，又建立持久的全球和平。这其实从二战以来一直是建制派的主流思想。

turns.en: Special Providence came out right around the time of 911. And people at that time weren't really aware that there was anything but Hamilton and Wilson.
turns.zh: 《Special Providence》正好在 911 前后出版。那时候人们其实并没意识到，除了 Hamilton 和 Wilson 还有别的东西。

turns.en: And then suddenly discovered, oh, wait a minute. There are these Jacksonians there who want to nuke Afghanistan or whatever came up after that.
turns.zh: 然后突然发觉：哦，等等，原来还有这些 Jacksonian——想要把 Afghanistan 核平、诸如此类，在那之后冒出来的人。

turns.en: I would say that Trump's coalition is a mix of Jeffersonians and Jacksonians, isolationists and hawks. You could say Vance as the isolationist champion in some ways and Rubio as the hawk.
turns.zh: 我会说，Trump 的联盟是 Jeffersonians 和 Jacksonians 的混合体：孤立主义者和鹰派。你可以说 Vance 在某种意义上是孤立主义的旗手，而 Rubio 是鹰派。

turns.en: Rubio is not interested in the United Nations or, you know, look at in Venezuela. Let's get rid of our enemy Maduro, but we're not going to make the restoration of democracy in Venezuela the key of everything, which someone like an Obama, I think, or a Biden would have tried much harder to do.
turns.zh: Rubio 对 United Nations 不感兴趣。你知道，看看 Venezuela：除掉我们的敌人 Maduro 可以，但我们不会把『恢复 Venezuela 民主』当成压倒一切的目标——而在我看来，像 Obama 或 Biden 那样的人，会花更大力气去做那件事。

turns.en: So on Ukraine, you can see the Jeffersonians are saying, well, this is not really our fight. Let's stay out of it while the Jacksonians are saying Russia's the enemy.
turns.zh: 所以在 Ukraine 问题上，你能看到 Jeffersonians 说：这其实不是我们的仗，别掺和；而 Jacksonians 说 Russia 就是敌人。

turns.en: Let's knock Putin and punch him in the nose while we can. They're all active today. Let me say one word more about this notion of tech Hamiltonians as a key faction that's emerged.
turns.zh: 趁现在能揍 Putin，就揍他个鼻青脸肿。今天这些派别全都活跃着。关于『科技汉密尔顿主义者』（tech Hamiltonians）作为一个涌现出来的关键派别，我还想再说一句。

turns.en: Typically, tech and the government were in my career different concepts. One of the biggest things that happened in modern American history is the mutual discovery of tech and government.
turns.zh: 在我的职业生涯里，科技界和政府历来是不同的概念。而在现代 US 史上，发生的最重大的事情之一，就是科技界与政府的相互发现。

turns.en: In the 1990s, which was back in the old end of history, end of nations, companies would say, oh, I'm not an American company. I'm a global company, right?
turns.zh: 1990 年代，那是『历史终结』、『国家终结』的老年代，公司会说：哦，我不是 US 公司，我是全球公司，对吧？

turns.en: And nowhere was that stronger than in the world of tech, where Google has no boundaries. The cyber world is completely different. All of that stuff is irrelevant to us.
turns.zh: 这种心态没有哪里比科技界更强：Google 没有边界，赛博世界完全不同，那些东西对我们毫无意义。

turns.en: Washington, they don't even understand us, and we will just do what we do today. Tech is actually the locus of international great power competition and China's attempt to build a tech-ness sphere that can dominate the American tech-ness sphere to American tech companies.
turns.zh: 华盛顿那帮人甚至不了解我们，我们只管照自己的方式干就行。科技其实已经成为国际大国竞争的场域——以及 China 试图建立一个足以压制 US 科技生态的科技势力范围，这对 US 的科技公司而言——

turns.en: This is really critical to your business, but also to the American state, American government. It's critical to power and independence. Much I think to the surprise of both the tech world and the political world, they've been driven in on each other.
turns.zh: ——这对你的生意至关重要，但对 US 国家、US 政府也至关重要，对权力和独立自主都至关重要。我想，无论是科技界还是政界，双方都在惊讶中被赶到了彼此身上。

turns.en: And there's a kind of renationalization of tech and of the economy that we see. And the tech folks, and you may know better, certainly Jeremy understands them a lot better than I do.
turns.zh: 于是我们看到一种科技和经济的『再国家化』。至于科技圈的人——你可能更了解，Jeremy 肯定比我看他们看得透得多。

turns.en: But my sense is that when the tech folks think about what are their economic interests, they're different from what you might call a legacy multinational, the post-World War II, that are basically global trading and manufacturing companies.
turns.zh: 但我的感觉是，当科技圈的人盘算自己的经济利益时，他们和你所谓的老牌跨国公司不一样——二战后那批公司，本质上是全球贸易和制造公司。

turns.en: I make cars from things I import from all over the world. I have factories all over the world that make cars. So for these companies, free trade is the essence of their business.
turns.zh: 『我用从世界各地进口的零件造车，在全球各地设厂造车。』所以对这类公司来说，自由贸易是其商业的本质。

turns.en: I need financial markets, I need labor markets, and I need manufactured goods markets that are seamless and open. As Tom Friedman put it, I need a flat earth.
turns.zh: 我需要无缝开放的金融市场、劳动力市场和制成品市场。正如 Tom Friedman 说的，我需要一张平坦的世界。

turns.en: But if you're a tech company, you don't. Alphabet is not importing and exporting a lot of goods, even something like immigration, which is if you're a hotel company or a construction company, having hard-working, cheap migrant labor is pretty important to your business model.
turns.zh: 但如果你是科技公司，你就不需要这些。Alphabet 并不大量进出口商品。甚至像移民这件事——如果你是酒店公司或建筑公司，勤奋便宜的移民劳工对你的商业模式相当重要。

turns.en: If you're a Silicon Valley company, and suddenly there's no more unskilled labor crossing from Mexico, the cost of your janitorial and gardening services rises 30%.
turns.zh: 如果你是硅谷公司，忽然没有非熟练劳工从 Mexico 越境过来了，你的保洁和园艺服务成本上升 30%。

turns.en: So what? You're much more concerned about security of supply chain, security of intellectual property, and I think increasingly companies are starting to realize that they need their employees to be patriotic.
turns.zh: 那又怎样？你更在乎的是供应链安全、知识产权安全。而且我想，越来越多的公司开始意识到：他们需要自己的员工是爱国的。

turns.en: That is, your employees need to think it's an evil sin to sell IP to China. Your coworkers will rat you out in a heartbeat if they think you're doing something like that.
turns.zh: 也就是说，你的员工得认为『把 IP 卖给 China』是一件邪恶的罪恶。一旦同事觉得你在干这种事，他们会毫不犹豫把你举报了。

turns.en: The economic agenda of the tech sector of the business world and the kind of cultural political attitude is changing. Because again, with the legacy multinationals, I want to have a completely international workforce.
turns.zh: 商界里科技板块的经济议程，以及那种文化政治心态，正在发生变化。因为再对比一下老牌跨国公司：我要的是一支完全国际化的员工队伍。

turns.en: I don't want it to matter whether my employees are from Sri Lanka or Taipei or wherever. I need interchangeable units that I can plug in anywhere.
turns.zh: 我不希望员工来自 Sri Lanka 还是 Taipei 还是别的地方这件事有任何影响。我需要可以互换的单元，插到哪儿都能用。

turns.en: If you take a big step back with all of this context and just think about global power, I feel like almost the whole world has decided that it's the Americans and the Chinese that have any real power or are contenders to be the powerful nation of the next period of time.
turns.zh: 把这些全部背景拉远一点，单看全球权力，我的感觉是：几乎全世界都已经认定，真正握有权力的、或者下一个时期可能成为强国候选的，只有 US 人和 Chinese。

turns.en: What are the other interesting sources of power that have your interest and curiosity? With all of the attention on just these two, we'll keep talking plenty more about these two as well, of course, but what other areas of power are most interesting to you right now?
turns.zh: 还有哪些有意思的权力来源让你感兴趣、让你好奇？当然，聚光灯全打在这两家身上之后，我们还会继续聊很多他们俩的话题——但此时此刻，你觉得最有意思的其他权力板块是什么？

turns.en: I've gotten very interested in India. I've been lucky enough to get to know a number of the folks that are close to the BJP and the RSS, which is the kind of Hindu nationalist group that helped to create the BJP.
turns.zh: 我最近对 India 非常感兴趣。我有幸结识了不少贴近 BJP 和 RSS 的人——RSS 大致是一个印度教民族主义团体，曾帮助创建了 BJP。

turns.en: This is a group of people who, 100 years ago, they see five guys in a house and they've now built this mass movement that has something like 86,000 small groups around India that meet weekly.
turns.zh: 一百年前，这拨人还在一栋房子里碰头的五个人，如今已经建成一场群众运动，在全 India 有大约 86,000 个每周聚会的小组。

turns.en: They're an incredibly dynamic political force. They powered Modi. They have very strong ideas about what India should be, what makes a country.
turns.zh: 他们是一支极其有活力的政治力量，Modi 是他们推上去的。他们对 India 应该成为什么、一个国家何以成为国家，有非常强烈的想法。

turns.en: India is now the most populous country in the world. India has been pretty successful at developing a tech industry. It's not in the frontier of AI.
turns.zh: India 现在是世界第一人口大国。India 在发展科技产业上颇为成功。虽然它目前还不在 AI 的最前沿。

turns.en: I think it may get there faster than people think, and it has its own sharply different view of what the world should be like. Which is what?
turns.zh: 我觉得它可能比人们想象得更快抵达前沿。而它对世界应该是怎样一幅图景，有自己鲜明的不同看法。什么样的看法？

turns.en: Multi-polar, but not in the Chinese way. Jay Shankar, who's the foreign minister of India, once said that China is a revisionist power. India is a reformist power, that India is not really happy with the global status quo.
turns.zh: 多极，但不是 China 那种多极。India 外长 Jaishankar 说过：China 是修正主义强国，India 是改革主义强国——India 对全球现状并不真的满意。

turns.en: In the United Nations system, India with 1.4 billion people in nuclear weapons has exactly as many votes in the General Assembly as Liechtenstein or Luxembourg.
turns.zh: 在 United Nations 体系里，拥有 14 亿人口和核武器的 India，在联大的票数跟 Liechtenstein 或 Luxembourg 一模一样。

turns.en: One vote. It's ridiculous, and there's a certain kind of Western domination to the way a lot of international life is organized, because it was basically organized by the Europeans and the Americans at a time when nobody else really had much of a standing.
turns.zh: 就一票。这很荒谬。而大量国际生活的组织方式里有一种西方主导在——因为它们基本是 Europeans 和 Americans 设计的，那时候别的谁基本没什么地位。

turns.en: There are a lot of changes they want to make, but they really don't see the kind of Chinese autocratic top-down approach as possible for India or also good for the world.
turns.zh: 他们想改的东西很多，但他们真的不认为 China 那种专制、自上而下的做法适用于 India，或者对世界是好事。

turns.en: They're an interesting power with different ideas, and I'm very much looking to see how that develops. I think the Islamic world, again, we are seeing the world of Islam.
turns.zh: 他们是一支带着不同理念的有趣力量，我非常想看看这条路怎么走。还有 Islamic 世界——同样，我们正在目睹的是一个变化中的 Islam 世界。

turns.en: It ranges from super sophisticated scholars and intellectuals and writers to jihadis in North Africa with machetes torching huts or something.
turns.zh: 它跨度极大：上到极有修养的学者、知识分子、作家，下到 North Africa 拿着砍刀烧村屋的圣战分子。

turns.en: All of this range, it's an immense civilization, but as a force in the world, there's more of it, it's becoming stronger. Understanding how it's changing, how the culture in the Gulf states and Turkey is changing and developing, I think the Industrial Revolution forced societies to become similar to each other, because if you're going to have big manufacturing plants, big infrastructure trains, highways, airports, all of this, there are certain things you just have to do institutionally
turns.zh: 这么一大片光谱，是一个庞大的文明；而作为世界中的一股力量，它分量更重、变得更强。理解它在如何变化、Gulf states 和 Turkey 的文化在如何变化发展，非常重要。我想，工业革命迫使社会彼此趋同——因为你要搞大制造厂、大基建，火车、公路、机场，所有这些，你在制度上——

turns.en: and organizationally that tend to kind of force you toward what we would think of as a European Western way of life and politics. The Information Revolution enables countries to use their own cultures, languages, and so on as platforms, and Turkey is more Turkish, it's less like Europe now than it was 25 years ago.
turns.zh: ——和组织上就必须做某些事，而这些事往往会把你推向我们所理解的那种 European、Western 的生活与政治方式。但信息革命让各国能用自己的文化、语言等等作为平台。Turkey 变得更 Turkish 了——它今天比 25 年前更不像 Europe。

turns.en: India is becoming, I think Japan is becoming more Japanese, so that in the Industrial Revolution, there was a tendency toward convergence of the great civilizations.
turns.zh: India 也是——我觉得 Japan 也在变得更 Japanese。所以在工业革命时代，各大文明有一种趋同的倾向。

turns.en: Now I think we're seeing a divergence. I'm not sure I fully understand the reason why that is. Can you explain it a little bit more? MTV, when it first went into Latin America, it was showing American rock videos on there, and everybody said, oh, this is going to be the end of indigenous Latin culture and so on.
turns.zh: 而现在，我觉得我们看到的是分异。我不太确定完全理解原因。你能多讲讲吗？MTV 刚进 Latin America 的时候，放的都是 American 摇滚 MV，大家都说：哦，本土的 Latin 文化要完了，云云。

turns.en: But before long, they weren't showing many American videos at all, because local artists were able really in a pretty cheap way to have their own music, their own videos that responded to those sensibilities.
turns.zh: 但没过多久，上面就基本不放多少 American MV 了，因为本地艺人能用相当低的成本做出自己的音乐、自己的 MV，回应本地人的审美。

turns.en: So I think we're seeing a lot of that now, where instead of having to be on the main line programming of global programming, you're much freer to go off into your own civilization.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，如今我们正在大量看到这种情形：不必再挤在全球主流节目的干线上，你可以更自由地退回到自己的文明里去。

turns.en: In that structure, I'm sure AI just pours fuel on that fire, what scares you the most? As you think about the global power dynamics, and I'm assuming your vision of the future that's optimistic would be progress and prosperity or something, what most would get in the way of the kind of future that you'd want to see?
turns.zh: 在这样一种格局里，AI 无疑是在火上浇油。你最害怕什么？想想全球权力动态——我猜你对未来的乐观图景大概是进步与繁荣什么的——最可能挡在你想看到的那种未来路上的，是什么？

turns.en: A lot of things. The Industrial Revolution was in the long run a pretty good thing, but it had little side effects like the Communist Party, the killing of 100 million people, World War I, World War II, Reign of Terror.
turns.zh: 很多东西。工业革命长期看是挺不错的事，但它的一些『小』副作用——像共产主义运动、一亿人的死亡、一战、二战、Reign of Terror（恐怖统治）。

turns.en: Why were those necessarily side effects of the Industrial Revolution? Because I think the social stresses that come with these new technologies uprooting millions of peasants from the farms where they've lived forever and now they're in cities and they're getting exploited, yeah, discontent, and the old social institutions that used to manage discontent, legitimate the state, don't work as well in this new context.
turns.zh: 为什么这些必然是工业革命的副作用？因为我想，这些新技术带来社会压力——把千百万农民从祖祖辈辈生活的土地上连根拔起，把他们推进城市、任人剥削，于是就有不满。而过去那些管理不满、让国家合法化的旧社会制度，在这个新格局下不那么管用了。

turns.en: Everything is changing, everyone's heads are scrambled, and things happen. So I think the Information Revolution, which is like exactly, so I definitely see that.
turns.zh: 一切都在变，人人脑子都是乱的，于是事情就发生了。所以我想，信息革命——正是如此——这点我 definitely 看到了。

turns.en: But then I look at things like, somebody's one of the biggest geopolitical problems of the last 60 years has been nuclear proliferation continues to be obviously to this day.
turns.zh: 但接下来我再看这些东西：过去 60 年最大的地缘政治问题之一一直是核扩散，而且显然到今天依然是。

turns.en: But when I think about weapons of mass destruction in the future, obviously biology, cyber, all kinds of things, while we have not been able to completely stop the proliferation of nuclear weapons, you can usually tell when somebody's trying to build them, usually you have enough lead time to try to do something about it.
turns.zh: 但当我想到未来的大规模杀伤性武器——显然是生物、网络，各种各样的东西——虽然我们没能彻底阻止核武器的扩散，但你通常看得出有人在试图造它，通常你有足够的提前量去想办法应对。

turns.en: How could you verify whether somebody was abiding by some sort of cyber arms control agreement or bio weapons arms control when basically in a basement lab somewhere you can cook up a pathogen that could destroy half the planet.
turns.zh: 而如果基本在某个地下室的实验室里就能培育出一种能毁掉半个地球的病原体，你又怎么核查别人在不在遵守某种网络军控协议或者生物武器军控协议呢？

turns.en: The idea that we're going to have accelerating arms races in a condition with an almost utter lack of strategic trust, where you can't appeal to verifiability as a way of ensuring compliance.
turns.zh: 在几乎完全没有战略信任的条件下，军备竞赛还会加速——而你没法把『可核查性』当作确保履约的办法。

turns.en: I think it's a pretty serious problem. So I think the rapid and dynamic technological change across a whole range of disciplines and technologies is destabilizing the balance of power.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是相当严重的问题。所以我想，横跨一大片学科和技术的快速、剧烈的技术变迁，正在瓦解力量的平衡。

turns.en: And this I think does significantly increase the chance both of confrontation and ultimately even of war between great powers. Speaking of maybe Ukraine is the right flash point for this, but it does seem like there's been quite an evolution of non weapons of mass destruction, just regular old weapons.
turns.zh: 而我认为这显著增加了大国之间对抗、乃至最终战争的可能性。说到这个，也许 Ukraine 是合适的引爆点，但常规武器——非大规模杀伤性武器的那种老式武器——也确实发生了相当大的演变。

turns.en: This is a highly contested topic now because of the conflict in Iran and some reports that we've run out of certain types of munitions, even as the United States of America.
turns.zh: 因为 Iran 的冲突，这现在是高度争议的话题，甚至有报道说，即便是 United States of America，某些类型的弹药也已经打光了。

turns.en: What have you learned from the last several years of conflict about the nature of military technology weapons, their relative importance in the eye world and so on?
turns.zh: 过去几年这些冲突，让你对军事技术和武器的本质、它们在 AI 世界里的重要性等等，学到了什么？

turns.en: Unfortunately I've learned a lot because there's been a lot of war. The first time I went to Ukraine after the war, I went to this drone factory and it really was remarkable because in real time they were starting to get results from the battlefield and then they were adapted.
turns.zh: 不幸的是，我学到的很多，因为发生了太多战争。战后我第一次去 Ukraine 时，去了一家无人机工厂，那地方真的令人惊叹——因为战场上实时传来结果，他们就能实时改进。

turns.en: Hittering. But at that time it was a very simplistic stuff. They were like getting kids toy trucks and re-engineering them into ground drones that could put a landmine on a tank.
turns.zh: 不断迭代。不过那时候东西还很简陋。他们像是把小孩的玩具卡车重新改装成地面无人车，往坦克上安放地雷。

turns.en: I was back there a couple of months ago. The advances are just unbelievable. The intensity is the same, but the scope of change is amazing. I talked to people who said that they don't treat bullet wounds anymore.
turns.zh: 几个月前我又去了。进步简直难以置信。烈度还是那个烈度，但变化幅度惊人。我跟一些人聊，他们说现在已经不治枪伤了。

turns.en: It's all drones. The Ukraine war is no longer a battalion over here shooting at a battalion over there. With these drones you have this sort of gray kill zone, gray zone, where at most you'd have a couple of soldiers together.
turns.zh: 全是无人机。Ukraine 战争已经不再是一个营在这边朝那边一个营开火了。有了这些无人机，会出现一种灰色杀伤区、灰色地带，在那里最多只有两三个士兵凑在一起。

turns.en: One of the hardest problems in warfare now they tell me is you'll get somebody wounded. How do you evacuate someone who's wounded? They're having to build a new kind of ground drone that can go retrieve a body or a person and then cover them with a kind of metal shield and wheel them out.
turns.zh: 他们告诉我，如今作战中最难的问题之一是有人负伤——你怎么把伤员后送？他们不得不造一种新型地面无人车，能去把人或遗体拖回来，再用一种金属护罩盖住，推出去。

turns.en: But even to do this you need a whole team of drones working with this thing because they're looking for other drones that would try to attack this.
turns.zh: 可即便是干这件事，也需要一整个无人机群来配合这台无人车，因为要提防那些会试图攻击它的对方的无人机。

turns.en: They told me they had one soldier that it took them 63 days to get them evacuated after a wound. This is so unlike what war was even six years ago.
turns.zh: 他们告诉我，有个士兵负伤之后花了 63 天才把他后送出来。这和六年前的战争已经完全不一样了。

turns.en: And I asked myself too, how fast is the Pentagon learning if the tank and the rifle are becoming as obsolete as the cavalry charge and the sword?
turns.zh: 我也在问自己：如果坦克和步枪正在变成和骑兵冲锋、宝剑一样过时的东西，Pentagon 学得有多快？

turns.en: What kind of forces do we have? What kind of forces do you need? And again it changes every six months. Right now the Ukrainians have kind of a battlefield advantage that could flip.
turns.zh: 我们手里有什么样的部队？你需要什么样的部队？而且这个又是每六个月一变。眼下 Ukrainians 握有一种战场优势，而这随时可能翻转。

turns.en: And it's also for us as the power that has the most stuff, we're actually the most vulnerable to technological change because we've got so many tanks that the tank becomes useless.
turns.zh: 而且，对我们这个家当最多的大国来说，我们其实对技术变迁最脆弱——因为我们囤了太多坦克，而坦克一旦变得没用，就是包袱。

turns.en: That's more of a problem for us than it is for somebody who's figured out the tank killer or Navy, you know, the Russian Navy on the Black Sea.
turns.zh: 这对我们来说，反而是比对那些琢磨出坦克杀手的人更大的难题。海军也一样——你知道，Russian Navy 在黑海。

turns.en: The Ukraine doesn't really have a Navy. They got a few little tiny boats, they don't have battleships and stuff. They have kept the Russian Navy out of the Black Sea with drones.
turns.zh: Ukraine 其实没有海军，只有几艘小得可怜的船，没有战列舰什么的。他们用无人机把 Russian Navy 挡在了黑海之外。

turns.en: Good news for Taiwan actually, but American power traditionally is about sea power to a very large extent. How does that change over time? We've gone from, you remember in the 90s, you look like you're just old enough to remember the 90s, they used to talk about the revolution and military affairs.
turns.zh: 其实这对 Taiwan 是好消息。但 American 的权力传统上在很大程度上海权。随着时间这会怎么变？我们已经从——你看起来刚好是记得 90 年代的年纪——90 年代他们老说的『军事事务革命』……

turns.en: We've shifted now, okay, there's this one thing happening. And once we've mastered and gotten used to it, then we're good to go. Now it's continuing revolutions in military affairs.
turns.zh: ——转到今天：哦，有这么一件事正在发生，一旦我们掌握并适应了，就万事大吉。如今则是『持续的军事事务革命』。

turns.en: That's something that I've learned about war by watching. What do you think is the most likely thing to happen in Taiwan? Well, the Chinese, Xi Jinping, I think is committed to trying to get it.
turns.zh: 这是我旁观战争学到的一点。你觉得 Taiwan 最可能发生什么？嗯，Chinese，Xi Jinping——我想他下决心要把它拿下。

turns.en: I don't think he actually has an alarm clock by his bed that will ring on the day that has to happen. The Chinese, I think, need a very high probability of success to commit themselves past a certain point because failure would be catastrophic for whoever launched it.
turns.zh: 我倒不觉得他床头真有个闹钟、到那天就会响。我想，Chinese 需要极高的成功概率才会把自己押过某个节点，因为对发起者来说，失败将是灾难性的。

turns.en: But there are a lot of steps in between an invasion and doing nothing. And we see the Chinese, I think they're trying to get themselves into a position where they could have a soft blockade, they could give the orders that any ship that wants to go to Taiwan first has to stop at a Chinese port and go through a customs clearing process to assert sovereignty and so on and make it difficult for ships that don't do that.
turns.zh: 但在全面入侵和什么都不做之间，有很多中间步骤。我们看到 Chinese——我想——正试图让自己处在能实施软封锁的位置：下令任何开往 Taiwan 的船都得先到 Chinese 港口停一下、过一遍海关清关，以此宣示主权等等，而不照做的船就举步维艰。

turns.en: They'll be looking for things that fly just under the radar that don't actually cause us to really respond, but which alter the situation in their favor.
turns.zh: 他们会寻找那些贴着雷达底线飞的动作——不会真正引发我们的强力回应，却能把局势朝有利于他们的方向改变。

turns.en: So I see them moving in that kind of way. The big new factor is that the Japanese have woken up and the Japanese would see Chinese control of Taiwan as a direct threat to Japanese independence.
turns.zh: 所以我看到的是他们在朝这个方向走。而最大的新变数是：Japanese 醒了。Japanese 会把 Chinese 控制 Taiwan 视为对 Japan 独立的直接威胁。

turns.en: I mean, they really see this. And so they are much more engaged. They're only beginning. They're raising their defense spending, they're rethinking their doctrine, they're beginning to kind of reshape their culture around the new strategic environment.
turns.zh: 他们是真看明白了，所以投入得多得多。而这只是开始：他们正在提高国防开支，重新思考学说，并开始围绕新的战略环境重塑自己的文化。

turns.en: Historically, the Japanese have actually been pretty good at changing direction when they genuinely feel threatened or feel the need to change in some way.
turns.zh: 历史上，Japanese 其实相当擅长掉头转向——当他们真切感到威胁、或者觉得必须以某种方式改变的时候。

turns.en: How this works out, I don't see, but I think it's one of the things people really need to keep an eye on is how fast do the Japanese come up the learning curve?
turns.zh: 这会怎么收场我看不准，但我觉得人们真正需要盯住的一件事是：Japanese 沿学习曲线爬得有多快？

turns.en: How serious does it turn out they really are about their own defense? And how does that affect China's calculations in Taiwan? If Japan is a new and complicating issue for them.
turns.zh: 他们对自身防务到底认真到什么程度？这又如何影响 Chinese 在 Taiwan 问题上的算盘？Japan 会成为一个对 Chinese 而言新增的、复杂化的变量。

turns.en: If I combine all these things, the changing forces of power, technology, military technology, all the things we've talked about with your observation that politics in the future is going to be more personal, are there any other rates of change, things changing in the world that we haven't talked about yet that you think are especially important for what the future will look like?
turns.zh: 如果我们把这些全都合起来——权力、技术、军事技术的变化之力，我们聊过的所有话题，加上你的观察：未来的政治会更个人化——那么还有什么别的变革速率、别的我们正在变化但还没谈到的东西，你觉得对未来图景特别重要吗？

turns.en: There were three basic classes in American society during the kind of post-World War II era of stability, and they spread a lot in the rest of the world.
turns.zh: 二战后那个稳定的年代，US 社会有三个基本阶级，而且它们很大程度上扩散到了世界其他地方。

turns.en: One was an industrial working class, which is kind of more or less in stable jobs with color. Yeah, exactly. Often organized in unions. They had a very pragmatic political attitude, and they were economically focused.
turns.zh: 一个是产业工人阶级，大体上都有稳定的工作、属于蓝领。对，正是。他们往往组织在工会里，政治上非常务实，注意力在经济上。

turns.en: And political competition between the left and the right was who can figure out how to raise living standards for the workers better. And that kind of centered politics on a fairly rational basis.
turns.zh: 左右两派的政治竞争，就是谁能更好地找到提高工人生活水平的办法。这就把政治锚定在一个相当理性的基础上。

turns.en: Then you had the business class, and by the 1940s and 50s, it was no longer the founders, the John D. Rockefeller originally, or the first J.P. Morgan.
turns.zh: 然后是商业阶级。到 1940、50 年代，他们已经不是创始人了——不再是当初的 John D. Rockefeller，也不是初代的 J.P. Morgan。

turns.en: It was grandsons, and it was publicly traded companies, professional managers. And so there was a kind of institutionalization of business. That was also the era of these very regulated monopolies and oligopolies.
turns.zh: 而是孙子辈，是上市公司、职业经理人。于是商业有一种制度化。那也是受严格管制的垄断和寡头时代。

turns.en: So there's one font company, a limited number of airlines, the three networks, very structured business world. And then between them, this organized, rationally focused working class and organized, regulated, publicly managed business class.
turns.zh: 所以只有一家电话公司，数量有限的几家航空公司，三大电视网，一个高度结构化的商业世界。然后介于两者之间——一边是有组织、理性导向的工人阶级，一边是有组织、受管制、公众管理的商业阶级。

turns.en: You had this expert class, the technocrats, the administrators, and so on, who according to the dictates of the best social science, peer-reviewed social science, were like making the decisions, regulate the businesses so they don't get too greedy, but also keep the workers from being so demanding that the whole system collapses, et cetera.
turns.zh: 中间站着专家阶级——技术官僚、行政管理者等等。他们按照最好的、经过同行评审的社会科学的指示来做决策：管住企业别太贪婪，但也别让工人索求无度、把整个体系搞塌，如此等等。

turns.en: And they were the balancing group. I would say in American society today, all three of those classes are in total disarray. And yet we are facing a whole series of very serious changes, perplexities.
turns.zh: 他们是平衡各方的那一群人。而我想说，今天的 US 社会，这三个阶级全都乱作一团。可我们面对的是整整一系列非常严重的变化和困惑。

turns.en: What do we do about AI? Just being one of many. We're not organized to answer these in the old ways. So we are really out at sea. And because America has been for so long and still I think remains the only potential pillar of global stability in organization, the internal incoherence of America faced with all of these changes can't help but undermine any chances of global stability.
turns.zh: 对 AI 我们该怎么办？这只是众多问题之一。我们已无法用老办法组织起来回答这些问题，所以我们真的漂泊在海上。而因为 US 长期以来、而且我认为今天仍然是全球稳定唯一潜在的组织支柱，US 面对这一切变化时的内部失序，必然削弱全球稳定的任何可能。

turns.en: So I think what that means is for people like you and me and maybe our listeners in the show a tremendously heavy responsibility to try to figure out answers and see some path through this and try to build a new kind of American politics and social order that can allow us once again to be reasonably stable for ourselves and then project that globally.
turns.zh: 所以我想，这意味着，对你我这样的人、对节目的听众们，有一份非常沉重的责任：想办法找出答案，看出一条穿越的路，尝试建设一种新的 US 政治与社会秩序，让我们再一次对自己而言相对平稳，并把这种稳定投射到全世界。

turns.en: What do you think against that backdrop it's going to mean or does mean to be an American? If all of that is changing, what does it mean? Think about being American in different ways.
turns.zh: 在这样的背景下，你觉得——或者现在就意味着——做一个 US 人会是什么？如果这一切都在变，那意味着什么？

turns.en: They have for a long time. You hear a lot of people talk these days about America as a country founded on ideas. Honestly, I think I was maybe in college before I met anybody who thought that way.
turns.zh: 做 US 人的方式有很多，而且很久以来就如此。如今你常听到人们说 US 是一个建立在理念之上的国家。说实话，我想我大概到上大学才第一次遇到持这种看法的人。

turns.en: From the south and down there you sort of thought, well, I'm an American because everybody I know is American. My family as long as I have any idea who the heck they were, they're Americans.
turns.zh: 在南方，在那一带，你的想法大致是：我是 US 人，因为我认识的每个人都是 US 人。我们家，只要我知道他们到底是谁，他们就是 US 人。

turns.en: I'm an American the same way a Frenchman is French or a Turkish Turk because I believe in America. But because I'm here and no one else would have me and it's like, this is it.
turns.zh: 我做 US 人的方式，就像法国人之为法国人、土耳其人之为土耳其人——不是因为我信仰 US，而是因为我就在这儿，别的谁都不肯收留我——事情就是这样。

turns.en: But there really are other people who love America and contribute to America who experience yes, it's a country of ideas and we are a pluralistic country in this way.
turns.zh: 但确实也有别的人，他们热爱 US、为 US 做出贡献，他们真切体会到：是的，这是一个理念之国，而我们在这一点上是一个多元的国家。

turns.en: And I don't myself feel more American than somebody that was naturalized last week. I think for me in some ways the sort of meeting ground between identity and ideas, honestly, it's the pledge of allegiance.
turns.zh: 我自己并不觉得我比一个上星期才入籍的人更像 US 人。对我而言，身份与理念的交汇之处，说实话，就是那段效忠宣誓（Pledge of Allegiance）。

turns.en: I pledge allegiance to the flag of the United States of America and to the Republic for which it stands, one nation indivisible under God with liberty and justice for all.
turns.zh: 我宣誓效忠美利坚合众国国旗，效忠它所象征的共和国：一个在上帝之下、不可分割的国度，人人享有自由与正义。

turns.en: And I would say anybody who says that and means it is an American. Very remarkable, huh? Well written. It's good. It's good. Your finance team isn't losing money on big mistakes.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，任何人只要说出这段话并且是认真的，他就是 US 人。这段真了不起，对吧？写得好。很好，很好。你的财务团队并不是在大错误上亏钱的——

turns.en: It's leaking through a thousand tiny decisions nobody's watching. Ramp puts guardrails on spending before it happens. Real time limits, automatic rules, zero firefighting.
turns.zh: ——而是从一千个没人盯着的小决定里流失掉的。Ramp 在花出去之前先给开支设好护栏：实时限额、自动规则、零救火。

turns.en: Try it at ramp.com slash invest. As your business grows, Banta scales with you, automating compliance and giving you a single source of truth for security and risk.
turns.zh: 到 ramp.com/invest 试试。随着业务增长，Vanta 与你同步扩展，把合规自动化，为安全与风险提供单一真相源。

turns.en: Learn more at Vanta.com slash invest. Ridgeline offers one unified platform that automates away the complexity across portfolio accounting, reconciliation, reporting, trading, compliance and more all at scale.
turns.zh: 详情见 Vanta.com/invest。Ridgeline 提供一个统一平台，把组合核算、对账、报告、交易、合规等等的复杂性在规模化的同时全部自动化。

turns.en: Schedule a demo at Ridgeline.ai. Every investment firm is unique and generic AI chatbots don't understand your process. Rogu is built by finance professionals.
turns.zh: 在 Ridgeline.ai 预约演示。每家投资公司都独一无二，而通用的 AI 聊天机器人不懂你的流程。Rogo 由金融专业人士打造。

turns.en: It's connected to your data, learns your process and quickly produces client ready outputs. Check them out at rogu.com slash invest. The best AI and software companies from open AI to cursor to perplexity use WorkOS to become enterprise ready overnight, not in months.
turns.zh: 它接入你的数据，学习你的流程，快速产出可以直接交给客户的成果。到 rogo.com/invest 看看。从 OpenAI 到 Cursor 再到 Perplexity，最好的 AI 和软件公司都用 WorkOS 一夜之间达到企业级就绪，而不是等上几个月。

turns.en: Visit WorkOS.com to skip the unglamorous infrastructure work and focus on your product. One thing I haven't asked about that I'm deeply curious about as I'm sure everyone is is your interpretation of what's going on in the Middle East, both with Iran, with Israel, with all the other key players where alliances seem to be shifting around for the first time in a long time.
turns.zh: 访问 WorkOS.com，跳过那些不起眼的基建活儿，专注你的产品。有一件事我一直没问，而且我深深好奇——我保证大家也一样——就是你对 Middle East 局势的解读：Iran、Israel，还有所有其他关键玩家，那里的联盟似乎多年来第一次在重新洗牌。

turns.en: How do you interpret what's happening? What are the deeper currents and messages that you're focused on? A lot of things obviously going on in the Middle East.
turns.zh: 你怎么解读正在发生的事？你关注的深层暗流、深层信号是什么？Middle East 显然有太多事情在发生。

turns.en: One background to a lot of stuff is just the sort of collapse of Arab nationalism and kind of Arab identity as an organizing force in the Middle East.
turns.zh: 很多事情背后的一条主线，就是 Arab 民族主义、以及作为 Middle East 组织性力量的 Arab 认同，正在坍塌。

turns.en: In the 1950s, Nasser and Egypt were the great pillars of Arab identity and Pan-Arabism. After the 67 war, they took a hit, but you would still have countries like Syria, Iraq, even for a while under Qaddafi, Libya aspiring to that mantle.
turns.zh: 1950 年代，Nasser 和 Egypt 是 Arab 认同与泛 Arab 主义的顶梁柱。67 年战争之后他们受到重挫，但像 Syria、Iraq，甚至 Qaddafi 治下一段时间的 Libya，仍然想接过那面大旗。

turns.en: If we look at what happened, Iraq collapsed, certainly America had a lot to do with that. Syria collapsed without America having a lot to do with it.
turns.zh: 看看后来发生了什么：Iraq 垮了，这当然和 America 有很大关系；Syria 也垮了，这倒没多少是 America 的作为。

turns.en: So Iran, as a non-Sunni, non-Arab power, had created what people call that, Shia Crescent from Lebanon, Syria, Iraq into Iran. While that, thanks to sort of Israel primarily since October 7, that's broken up.
turns.zh: 于是，作为非 Sunni、非 Arab 的强国，Iran 建立了人们所说的那条什叶派新月地带（Shia Crescent）——从 Lebanon、Syria、Iraq 一路连进 Iran。而这条线，主要得益于 Israel 的努力，在 October 7 之后被打断了。

turns.en: But what hasn't broken up is the underlying weakness of the Arab world is still there. And you have the Gulf states that are very effective in many ways and are using their oil and their money very effectively, but they still can't defend themselves from Iran.
turns.zh: 但没被打断的是——Arab 世界底层的那个虚弱依然故我。你看 Gulf states，在很多方面非常有效率，非常有效地利用着自己的石油和金钱，但他们仍然防不住 Iran。

turns.en: They still, without outside help, they cannot stand. And that leads to the Strait of Hormuz in that region, which remains incredibly important for the economic stability and health of the world.
turns.zh: 没有外力帮忙，他们仍然站不起来。这就牵出该地区的那条 Hormuz 海峡——它对全世界的经济稳定与健康仍然无比重要。

turns.en: That is in chaos. If the United States or some other power doesn't hold Iran back in some way, it has a hegemony over the oil resources in the Middle East in a way that allows them to blackmail a lot of people economically and provides them with the kinds of resources that would not certainly be used to our benefit.
turns.zh: 那里正在一片混乱。如果 US 或者其他某个大国不以任何方式牵制 Iran，Iran 就会对 Middle East 的石油资源形成霸权——让他们能在经济上勒索很多人，并为他们提供那些肯定不会用来造福我们的资源。

turns.en: Israel, I think, may have hoped that it could kind of bear the weight of being a counter-hegemon to Iran. Israel is too small and too alien to the rest of the Middle East to really play that role effectively, I think.
turns.zh: Israel，我想，或许曾希望自己能扛得住作为 Iran 反霸权制衡者的分量。但 Israel 太小，又与 Middle East 其他地方太隔膜，我认为恐怕演不好这个角色。

turns.en: Since Obama, the United States has been fundamentally unwilling to do that itself. And we want to kick the can down the road. We want to find some other way other than us putting down a red line that we enforce with Iran.
turns.zh: 自 Obama 以来，US 从根本上就不愿意自己来做这件事。我们想把罐子往前踢，想找到别的办法，而不是由我们给 Iran 划一条我们会执行的底线。

turns.en: History doesn't give us a choice. We stop Iran ourselves, or Iran asserts and maintains hegemony over the oil resources in the Middle East. Why have we been unaffected?
turns.zh: 历史不给我们选择：要么我们自己阻止 Iran，要么 Iran 确立并维持对 Middle East 石油资源的霸权。为什么我们一直不受影响？

turns.en: Obviously, we have vastly superior military capability or whatever. This is a specific question about Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, but also people used to call Afghanistan the graveyard of empires.
turns.zh: 我们当然有压倒性的军事实力什么的。这本是关于 Iran 和 Hormuz 海峡的具体问题，但人们过去也管 Afghanistan 叫『帝国的坟场』。

turns.en: Why do world powers seem to have such a difficult time being affected at all in the Middle East? Well, I think some of it is, which we've also seen with Russia, is the erosion of deterrence.
turns.zh: 为什么世界大国在 Middle East 似乎都很难被真正触动？嗯，我想部分原因——我们从 Russia 身上也看到了——是威慑的侵蚀。

turns.en: What you don't want to do is help Ukraine win a war with Russia. What you want is for Russia to feel that if they attack Ukraine, the consequences would be so terrible that it's just not worth doing it.
turns.zh: 你真正要的不是帮 Ukraine 打赢和 Russia 的战争，你要的是让 Russia 觉得：如果他们攻打 Ukraine，后果会严重到根本不值得动手。

turns.en: Anything other than deterrence involves long, difficult, expensive, divisive wars with uncertain outcomes and enormous costs. The decline of deterrence becomes a massive geopolitical problem overseas and a massive political problem at home.
turns.zh: 除了威慑之外的任何东西，都会拖入漫长、艰难、昂贵、撕裂、结局不确定、代价巨大的战争。威慑的衰落，对外变成巨大的地缘政治难题，对内变成巨大的政治难题。

turns.en: For example, right now, one of the real facts in the Strait is it's not even as important that Iran can hit a tanker with a drone as it is that Iran could put some drones on some desalinization plants and make the cities of the Gulf essentially uninhabitable.
turns.zh: 比如说，眼下海峡一带的一个真正的事实是：Iran 能用无人机打中油轮这件事的分量，其实还不如——Iran 能把一些无人机放在一些海水淡化厂边上，让 Gulf 的城市基本上无法居住。

turns.en: As long as that's the case, I'm not going to make big investments in the Gulf if I'm a foreign country. It's really, really scary. That means that these whole economic development plans that those countries have for their future political stability go up in smoke because it doesn't work.
turns.zh: 只要情况如此，假如我是外国，我就不会在 Gulf 进行大额投资，那实在太吓人了。这意味着这些国家为了未来政治稳定而制定的整套经济发展规划会化为乌有——因为这套东西行不通。

turns.en: The only way to preserve that is in some ways what we were doing in the Cold War in Europe, just saying to Russia, you cross that line, you invade West Berlin and holy hell breaks out.
turns.zh: 唯一能保住这一切的办法，在某种意义上就是我们在冷战时期在 Europe 做的那一套：直接告诉 Russia——你越过那条线、你入侵 West Berlin，那就天崩地裂。

turns.en: But I think as a country, we're not at the point where President of the United States can say it and mean it and have the public back him up.
turns.zh: 但我觉得，我们这个国家还没到那种地步——US 总统能说出这句话、言出必行，而且民众还Backing him up。

turns.en: For that, we need presidents who can explain to people, okay, this is how the world works, what Harry Truman did after World War II, for that matter what Franklin Roosevelt did in the fireside chats.
turns.zh: 要做到那点，我们需要这样的总统：能向人们讲清楚——好吧，世界就是这么运转的。这就是 Harry Truman 在二战后做的事，就此而言，也是 Franklin Roosevelt 在炉边谈话里做的事。

turns.en: Take the American people into your confidence. Have a clear vision of what you're doing, why you're doing it. Be enough of a communicator to be able to put it across.
turns.zh: 把 US 人民纳入你的信任。对自己在做什么、为什么做，有清晰的愿景。并且要是一个够格的沟通者，能把这些传达出去。

turns.en: We haven't really had anybody do that in a very long time. What do you hope we do? What do you hope America's role is in the next 20 years? I hope we first of all figure out how to keep our balance as we enter the information revolution.
turns.zh: 我们其实已经很久没有真正出现这样的人了。你希望我们做什么？你希望 US 在未来 20 年扮演什么角色？首先，我希望我们在进入信息革命的时候，能学会站稳脚跟。

turns.en: That we figure out how to use the wealth and the resources the information revolution creates to deal with the stresses and problems that it inevitably causes and also draw from it the abundance that will keep the American people feeling like America's working, it's working for them.
turns.zh: 我希望我们搞明白，如何用信息革命创造的财富和资源去化解它必然造成的压力与问题，并从中汲取那种富足——让 US 人民觉得 US 运转得好，在为他们运转。

turns.en: The way things are going is basically a good thing. You have that going, then people will back an American president, an American foreign policy in a serious way.
turns.zh: 事情进展的方式基本上是一件好事。有了这个，人们就会认真地支持一位 US 总统、一种 US 的外交政策。

turns.en: And I think if you don't have that, if we don't do that, we lose ground in the information revolution to China and the tech race. We get challenged overseas and at home we're just rabid ferrets fighting with each other in a cage and that's just not pretty and not fun.
turns.zh: 而我认为，如果你做不到这点、我们不做到这点，我们会在信息革命、在这场科技竞赛中输给 China、节节失地。我们在海外受人挑战，在国内则像关在笼子里互相撕咬的疯貂——那既不好看，也不好玩。

turns.en: And if we can get that going, then I think we act purposefully. We say we don't want any great power dominating Europe. We don't want any great power dominating Asia and we don't want any power able to interrupt the flow of oil in and out of the Middle East on commercial terms and we build the alliances and the relationships that do it.
turns.zh: 如果我们能让那件事运转起来，那么我想我们就能有目的地行动：我们声明不希望任何大国主导 Europe，不希望任何大国主导 Asia，不希望任何强权有能力打断 Middle East 石油按商业条款的进出流动——然后我们为此去建设同盟和关系。

turns.en: I don't think that is an unsustainable ask. Germany and Japan in particular have a lot of resources and a lot of ability, but also our problem in Asia is not that China is so big and the rest of Asia has fallen behind.
turns.zh: 我不觉得这是一个无法承受的诉求。Germany 和 Japan 尤其拥有大量资源和能力。而且我们在 Asia 的问题，并不是 China 太大而 Asia 其他地方落后了。

turns.en: In 1980, India's GDP was something like 60%, 65% of China's. Today it's about 17% of China's. That gap in a sense is the imbalance of power that sort of tempts China into thinking hegemony in Asia is really possible and also ensures that without us putting a really heavy weight on the balance scale, it can't be stopped.
turns.zh: 1980 年，India 的 GDP 大约相当于 China 的 60%、65%；今天它只有 China 的 17% 左右。这种落差在意义上就是权力的失衡——它诱惑着 China 以为在 Asia 搞霸权真的可行，也注定了：除非我们在天平上压上足够重的砝码，否则它是停不下来的。

turns.en: If we can create a world that there's room for others to prosper, that not only India but Indonesia and Vietnam are growing, I think what we're going to see is China will kind of reach this point of understanding that Asia is too big for China to eat.
turns.zh: 如果我们能创造一个让其他人也有繁荣空间的世界，让不只是 India，还有 Indonesia、Vietnam 都在增长，我想我们会看到，China 会走到这个认识：Asia 太大，China 吃不下。

turns.en: Nobody can eat it and so we need to learn to live with folks, which Germany has done in Europe. It's possible. And in the same way, if Russia is stopped in Ukraine and Ukraine goes like Poland and becomes a prosperous country in all of this, that door is closed without American soldiers fighting and dying to keep it closed.
turns.zh: 谁也吃不下，所以大家都得学会与邻共处——Germany 在 Europe 就是这么做的。这是可能的。同样，如果 Russia 在 Ukraine 被挡住，而 Ukraine 像 Poland 一样、在这一切之中变成一个繁荣的国家，那么那扇门就关上了——而不需要 US 士兵去战斗、去牺牲才守得住。

turns.en: So there is I think the potential for the kind of natural balance of power in these key theaters to emerge in a way that we can have the sort of world that is good for us economically and from a security point of view, but does not require an ever escalating defense budget and ever escalating series of American commitments.
turns.zh: 所以我想，在这些关键的战略场域，存在一种自然的权力平衡自行浮现的可能——如此我们就能拥有一个在经济上和安全上对我们都好的世界，而不必把国防预算不断拔高、不必让 US 的承诺不断加码。

turns.en: Is there anything especially unique you call it the information revolution? I would think about it maybe as the intelligence revolution, like to make it very specific to AI.
turns.zh: 这里面有没有什么是特别独特的？你把它叫信息革命；我倒是倾向于称之为智能革命，好让它更明确地指向 AI。

turns.en: Is there anything that you're thinking about that excites you most or worries you most about this very unique brand of technology in global affairs?
turns.zh: 在这套非常独特的技术之于全球事务这件事上，有没有什么你在思考的、最让你兴奋或最让你担忧的东西？

turns.en: Well, it is interesting how it seems at least for now to have simplified the international playing field. The people, as you were saying earlier, just they said there's America and there's China and there's no one else in the room.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，至少眼下，它似乎让国际牌桌简化了。正如你之前说的，人们就说：只有 America 和 China，房间里没有别人。

turns.en: First of all, I wonder how long that will last because originally there were two nuclear powers, America and Soviet Union and nobody else was in the room.
turns.zh: 首先，我不知道这种局面会持续多久，因为最初只有两个核大国——US 和 Soviet Union——房间里没有别人。

turns.en: But then a bunch of other people started getting into the room. Is AI more replicable? Are we going to start seeing other countries come up with their equivalent of these technologies that Chinese have obviously done it with less need for original skull sweat than we did?
turns.zh: 但后来一大批人开始走进房间。AI 是不是更容易被复制？我们会不会开始看到其他国家搞出这些技术的对等物——而 Chinese 显然已经做到了，而且比我们当初需要下的原创苦功少得多？

turns.en: Can third parties look comparing the US and China do more? So I'd be definitely watching that one. And there I think the Indians and the Europeans and the Israelis are all very interesting in that respect.
turns.zh: 第三方——拿 US 和 China 对比来看——还能做得更多吗？所以这一点我一定会盯着看。这方面我觉得 Indians、Europeans 和 Israelis 都很有意思。

turns.en: Israelis got their nuclear bomb just a couple of years, a few years after China. So look at that. I do think the whole question of AIs and national security decision making and deterrence is interesting because the whole goal of deterrence is you want to make the adversary believe that there's no question.
turns.zh: Israelis 的原子弹，就在 China 之后没几年、仅仅几年就搞出来了——看看这个。我确实觉得，AI 与国家安全决策、与威慑的整个问题很有意思，因为威慑的全部目标，就是让对手毫不怀疑——

turns.en: If I do X, they will do Y. They will be able to do Y and they are willing to do Y. Automating your foreign policy decision making process increases deterrence.
turns.zh: ——『如果我做 X，他们就会做 Y』：他们有能力做 Y，而且愿意做 Y。把外交决策流程自动化，会增强威慑。

turns.en: And so we've turned that over to the AI and if the AI thinks you're doing this, wham. And anything less than that is no, I'm leaving a human decision point because I might decide not to do it.
turns.zh: 于是我们把这件事交给 AI：只要 AI 判定你在做这件事，轰！而只要不那么彻底——『我留一个人工决策点，因为我可能决定不做』——威慑就打了折扣。

turns.en: That's interesting when you think about how that might play out in the world of deterrence and are we really willing to have the doomsday machine decide whether we're going to go to war or use nuclear weapons or something like that.
turns.zh: 想想这在威慑世界里会如何展开，就很有意思了：我们真的愿意让那台『末日机器』来决定我们打不打仗、要不要动用核武器之类的事吗？

turns.en: Very interesting and somewhat perplexing. Maybe to end on a positive note, what are you most excited about in the future? The list is almost endless.
turns.zh: 很有意思，也有点让人困惑。不如以积极的调子收尾：未来最让你兴奋的是什么？那份清单几乎写不完。

turns.en: When I think about the acceleration of medical research that's going to be coming, let's just look at what AI and generally advances in tech are doing in the field of medicine.
turns.zh: 当我想到即将到来的医学研究加速——就看看 AI 和整体技术进步正在医学领域做什么吧。

turns.en: The rate at which cures are being found are treatments. My friend Ben Sasse who was diagnosed with terminal pancreatic cancer, I mean he's still in a very bad situation.
turns.zh: 治愈方法和疗法被找到的速度。我的朋友 Ben Sasse 被诊断为晚期胰腺癌——他现在的处境仍然非常糟糕。

turns.en: But a drug that didn't exist a year ago is keeping him not just breathing but interacting with people and doing things, it is a stay of execution.
turns.zh: 但一种一年前还不存在的药，让他不仅还在呼吸，还能和人交流、还能做事——这是一次缓刑。

turns.en: But the point is I can look back at people in my own family who died of various conditions which would now if they had them be treatable and that's in one lifetime.
turns.zh: 重点是：我可以回望自己家族里那些死于各种病症的人——那些病放在今天本来是可以治的——而这一切就发生在人的一生之间。

turns.en: And I also believe that we're going to be seeing a cost revolution in health care that people will have 50 years from now better health care and cheaper health care than anybody has today.
turns.zh: 而且我也相信，我们即将看到一场医疗的成本革命：50 年后的人们，会得到比今天任何人都享有的都更好、都更便宜的医疗。

turns.en: I think this means that things like the federal deficit due to entitlement programs are actually solvable that we're going to have Medicare is going to be less of a drag and the seniors are going to get better care.
turns.zh: 我觉得这意味着：像福利项目造成的联邦赤字这类问题其实是可解的——Medicare 会成为更小的拖累，而老年人会得到更好的照护。

turns.en: So I think many of the problems that are driving us really crazy right now are actually amenable to solution and the solutions are appearing at a fast rate and that our biggest problem is that this cornucopia of wealth that the information revolution unlocks, the stuff is coming out of this cornucopia so fast we just don't know how to manage it.
turns.zh: 所以我想，眼下很多让我们抓狂的问题其实是可解的，解法正以很快的速度涌现。而我们最大的难题是：信息革命解锁的这一大聚宝盆——里面的财富涌出来的速度太快，我们还不知道怎么管理它。

turns.en: I am fundamentally optimistic that we are on the cusp of a unique era of human transformation and renewal and development and it's really exciting to be able to see it.
turns.zh: 从根本上，我是乐观的：我们正站在一个独特的人类转型、更新与发展时代的门槛上，而能亲眼看见这一切，真的令人兴奋。

turns.en: I've been reading your books and you're thinking and you're writing for so long it's such a thrill to do this together in person. When I do these I ask everyone the same final question, what is the kindest thing that anyone's ever done for you?
turns.zh: 我读你的书、你的思想、你的文字已经好久了，能和你这样当面一起做这期节目，真是太棒了。我做节目都会问所有人同一个最终问题：别人为你做过的最善良的一件事是什么？

turns.en: I mean less gal but the council on farm relations was just a magnificent mentor who when I would do something stupid would help me see it but also help me figure out the next step forward.
turns.zh: 这个嘛……Council on Foreign Relations 真是一位了不起的导师——我干了蠢事时，他会让我看见问题，同时也帮我找出往前走的那一步。

turns.en: I have had so much undeserved kindness from so many people in so many dimensions of life. Younger relatives now who put up with their endlessly boring, talkative, another one of those old war stories.
turns.zh: 从太多人身上、在太多个人生维度上，我领受了太多我并不配得的善意。现在年轻一辈的亲戚也容忍着我——那个永远讲不烦的唠叨老头，『又来一段当年那些陈年战争故事了』。

turns.en: Employers who keep me going put up with me. The Wall Street Journal Paul Gigo letting me be the global view columnist at the journal. I float on a sea of kindness and I don't know that it's easy to say there's one thing kinder than another, I've just been blessed.
turns.zh: 还有继续用我、容忍我的雇主们。《Wall Street Journal》的 Paul Gigot 让我在报上担任 Global View 专栏作家。我漂浮在一片善意的海洋上——我很难说哪件事比其他事更善良，我只是被眷顾了。
